hook.text: Nobody plans how many loaves of bread a city needs each day. Yet bakeries bake roughly the right amount. How?

buildup.text: Adam Smith called it the invisible hand. Individuals pursuing self-interest unintentionally benefit the whole society.

discovery.text: The baker bakes to earn money, not to feed the city. Yet competition and prices coordinate supply perfectly.

twist.text: The invisible hand has blind spots. It ignores externalities, public goods, and inequality.

climax.text: The invisible hand is powerful but imperfect. It coordinates brilliantly and fails where prices miss the full cost.

punchline.text: Self-interest coordinates supply. But markets need guardrails.

quiz.question: What does the invisible hand describe?
options: Individuals pursuing self-interest unintentionally benefiting society
